content:
Pakistani students have one of the strongest scholarship landscapes in the world — several flagship programmes explicitly reserve places for Pakistan, from Commonwealth and Chevening in the UK to Türkiye Bursları, GKS Korea, MEXT Japan, Stipendium Hungaricum and the ADB–Japan Scholarship. This guide puts every realistic 2027 route in one place, with typical application windows, funding levels and what each programme actually wants from Pakistani applicants.

The big scholarships open to Pakistanis

ScholarshipLevelFundingTypical window
Commonwealth Scholarships (UK)Master's, PhDFull fees + stipend + flightsOpens ~Sept, closes ~Oct–Nov 2026 for 2027
Chevening (UK)Master's (1 yr)Full fees + living allowanceAug–Nov 2026
Fulbright (USA, via USEFP)Master's, PhDFull funding + health coverTypically opens ~Feb; confirm with USEFP
Türkiye BurslarıBachelor's–PhDFull tuition + stipend + dorm + flightsJan–Feb 2027 (listing: closes 20 Feb 2027)
GKS (Korea)Bachelor's–PhDTuition + KRW 900,000/mo + airfareEmbassy track Feb–Mar 2027
MEXT (Japan)Bachelor's–PhDTuition + ¥143–145k/mo + flightsEmbassy track ~Apr–May; university track varies
Stipendium HungaricumBachelor's–PhDTuition + stipend + housing support~Jan 2027
Erasmus Mundus (EU)Master's€1,400/mo + travelOct 2026 – Feb 2027 by programme

Where funded positions actually are (from live listings)

Of the opportunities currently published on NextApply that accept applicants worldwide, the host-country distribution shows where Pakistani applicants can realistically compete for salaried doctoral and funded master's places:

Host countryLive worldwide-eligible positions
United Kingdom130
Netherlands91
Sweden38
Germany35
France26
Switzerland16
Australia15
Belgium13

Continental Europe's employed PhD model (Germany, Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland) is the highest-volume route for Pakistani master's holders: no separate scholarship needed — the position is the funding. Start from our guide to identifying funded PhDs that accept international students.

Pakistan-specific paperwork (start early)

  • HEC attestation of degrees and transcripts — required by several programmes and slow at peak times (weeks). Do it before application season, not during.
  • Passport validity: at least 6 months beyond intended travel; renew early if expiring.
  • Transcript equivalence: some programmes want IBCC/HEC or WES evaluation — our grade conversion guide explains the common scales.
  • English tests: IELTS/TOEFL booking queues in Pakistan fill months ahead; many European positions accept a Medium of Instruction certificate instead.

How to sequence a 2027 application year

  1. Now (Nov–Dec 2026): get HEC attestation moving; book IELTS if needed; shortlist 8–10 programmes across at least three countries.
  2. Dec 2026–Feb 2027: CSC, Türkiye Bursları (closes 20 Feb), GKS embassy track (mid-Feb), Stipendium Hungaricum, Erasmus Mundus deadlines, remaining Dutch/German positions.
  3. Feb–May 2027: Fulbright via USEFP, MEXT embassy track, university-track GKS, spring European positions.
  4. Interviews through spring: prepare with our interview guide — Chevening and Fulbright interviews are scripted around your essays; re-read them before every session.

Building the profile these programmes score highest

  • Leadership evidence (Chevening, Fulbright, Commonwealth): community work, campus societies, professional impact — the personal statement structure applies directly.
  • Research fit (PhD routes): name groups and papers, not just universities — see how to find and email supervisors.
  • Home-country impact: nearly every flagship programme weighs what you will do in Pakistan afterwards — make it concrete.

Questions applicants often ask

CGPA below 3.0 — is it over? No. Türkiye Bursları and CSC work with strong interviews and statements; several European universities admit on fit — see our low CGPA guide.

Can I apply to multiple scholarships at once? Yes — these programmes don't exclude each other; you can only accept one funded award.

Age limits? Türkiye Bursları and GKS have them; Commonwealth and Chevening do not; our age-limit list has the details.

Patterns in successful Pakistani applications

  • Two-country strategy: most winners apply to one "flagship" programme (Chevening, Commonwealth, Fulbright) and a parallel European track (Erasmus Mundus, Dutch/German positions) — the flagships are lottery-like, the European track is numbers-based and rewards volume.
  • The employed-PhD track is underused: Pakistani applicants over-index on named scholarships and under-apply to salaried positions in the Netherlands, Sweden, Germany and Switzerland — where 130+ UK and 91 Dutch worldwide-eligible positions are live right now. A funded position application takes an afternoon; a scholarship essay cycle takes months.
  • Work experience doubles your options: ADB-JSP (2+ years), Chevening (2+ years) and Fulbright both reward professional records — if you graduated recently, bank two years of strong work and reapply.
  • IELTS planning is the hidden deadline: test centres in Pakistan queue for weeks in summer; a December test date comfortably covers February deadlines.

Where to start this week

  1. Get HEC attestation moving — the single most common bottleneck for Pakistani applications abroad.
  2. Draft one master CV (our academic CV sample) — it serves every application.
  3. Shortlist across three tiers: 3 flagships (Commonwealth/Chevening/GKS), 3 mid-tier (Türkiye Bursları, Stipendium Hungaricum, CSC), 5+ European positions (search the NextApply listings by deadline).
  4. Book IELTS if any target needs it; otherwise request a Medium of Instruction letter from your university now.
